name.description: The name of the logging sink. Must be unique within the project. Names can contain only letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens.
name.rationale: Proper naming helps identify the purpose of log sinks and maintain organizational standards for security monitoring.

destination.description: The destination for the logs. Supported destinations include: `storage.googleapis.com/[GCS_BUCKET]`, `bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/[PROJECT_ID]/datasets/[DATASET]`, `pubsub.googleapis.com/projects/[PROJECT_ID]/topics/[TOPIC_ID]`, `logging.googleapis.com/projects/[PROJECT_ID]/locations/global/buckets/[BUCKET_ID]`, `logging.googleapis.com/projects/[PROJECT_ID]`. The writer associated with the sink must have access to write to the destination resource.
destination.rationale: Secure destination configuration ensures logs are stored in trusted, access-controlled environments for security monitoring.

filter.description: See [Advanced Log Filters](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/view/advanced_filters) for information on how to write a filter. The filter that determines which log entries are exported to the destination.
filter.rationale: Proper filtering ensures that security-relevant logs are captured while reducing noise and storage costs.

description.description: A description of the sink, which explains its purpose and what logs it captures. This helps maintain auditability of log routing.
description.rationale: Clear descriptions provide documentation but don't directly impact security configuration.
description.compliant: Exports security-related logs to BigQuery for analysis and monitoring

disabled.description: If set to true, the sink is disabled and does not export any log entries.
disabled.rationale: Unexpected disabling of security sinks can interrupt security monitoring and incident response capabilities.

project.description: The project ID where the sink should be created. If not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Proper project specification ensures sinks are created in the correct project context with appropriate access controls.

unique_writer_identity.description: If true, then a unique service account is created and used for this sink. If you wish to publish logs across projects or utilize `bigquery_options`, you must set `unique_writer_identity` to true.
unique_writer_identity.rationale: Unique writer identities provide better security isolation and auditability for cross-project log routing.

custom_writer_identity.description: A custom service account used to write the log entries. The format must be `serviceAccount:some@email`. This field can only be specified if you are routing logs to a destination outside this sink's project. If not specified, a Logging service account will automatically be generated.
custom_writer_identity.rationale: Custom writer identities allow for fine-grained control over permissions and audit trails for cross-project log routing.

bigquery_options.description: Options that affect sinks exporting logs to BigQuery.
bigquery_options.rationale: BigQuery options affect data organization but don't directly impact security.

use_partitioned_tables.description: By default, Logging creates dated tables based on the log entries' timestamps, e.g. `syslog_20170523`. With partitioned tables the date suffix is no longer present and [special query syntax](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/querying-partitioned-tables) has to be used instead. In both cases, tables are sharded based on UTC timezone.
use_partitioned_tables.rationale: Table partitioning affects query performance and cost but doesn't directly impact security.

exclusions.description: Log entries that match any of the exclusion filters are not exported. This allows fine-grained control over what logs are excluded from the sink.
exclusions.rationale: Proper exclusion configuration prevents security-relevant logs from being accidentally filtered out of security monitoring.

name.description: The name of the exclusion. Must be unique within the sink.
name.rationale: Proper naming helps identify the purpose of exclusions within security monitoring sinks.

description.description: A description of the exclusion, which explains why certain logs are being excluded from this sink.
description.rationale: Clear descriptions provide documentation but don't directly impact security.
description.compliant: Excludes health check logs to reduce noise in security monitoring

filter.description: See [Advanced Log Filters](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/view/advanced_filters) for information on how to write a filter. The filter that determines which log entries to exclude from the sink.
filter.rationale: Carefully crafted exclusion filters prevent security-relevant logs from being accidentally filtered out.

disabled.description: If set to true, the exclusion is disabled and does not exclude any log entries from the sink.
disabled.rationale: Unexpected enabling/disabling of exclusions can affect security monitoring by including sensitive data or excluding security-relevant logs.
